target.title: feat: add codexbar cookie refresh CLI command
target.body:
## Summary

Adds `codexbar cookie refresh --provider <name>` CLI command to force re-import of browser cookies for cookie-authenticated providers.

**Note:** Settings-pane refresh buttons (↻) split into a separate PR: **#2264**.

## Behaviour

- `codexbar cookie refresh --provider opencodego` — clears Keychain cache, re-imports from all supported browsers, stores fresh cookie
- `codexbar cookie refresh --all` — refreshes OpenCode and OpenCode Go
- Falls back gracefully when `importSession` fails (code-signing entitlements required)
- Supports `--format text|json`, `--json`, `--json-only`, `--pretty`
- Uses the provider's automatic browser import order (scans all installed browsers via `preferredBrowsers: []`)

## Verified Behaviour

### Evidence

See `docs/proof/cli-cookie-refresh-proof.md` for full test matrix.

Key results:

| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| `cookie refresh --provider opencodego` | ✅ JSON output: `"status": "cleared"` |
| Before: Keychain `cookie.opencodego` | `storedAt: 2026-07-17T18:25:50Z` |
| After: Keychain lookup | ❌ Not found (cache cleared) |
| After CodexBar.app refresh | ✅ Cookie re-imported with fresh `storedAt` |
| `--provider nonexistent` | ✅ `"Unknown provider: nonexistent"` |
| `--all` | ✅ Targets only OpenCode + OpenCodeGo |
| `--format json --pretty` | ✅ Valid JSON output |
| Build | ✅ `swift build` zero errors |

### End-to-end flow

```
CLI command                         CodexBar.app (menu bar)
┌──────────────────────┐            ┌─────────────────────┐
│ cookie refresh       │            │ auto-refresh detects │
│ --provider opencodego│            │ missing cache        │
│                      │            │                      │
│ ① Clear Keychain ✅  │  ──────→  │ ② SweetCookieKit     │
│ ② Import browser ❌  │  (fail)   │    import from Chrome │
│    (unsigned binary) │            │ ③ Store in Keychain  │
│ ③ Print "cleared"    │            │ ④ Refresh usage ✅   │
└──────────────────────┘            └─────────────────────┘
```

### Known Limitation

`OpenCodeCookieImporter.importSession()` requires code-signing entitlements unavailable in debug CLI builds. The command clears the cache and falls back — the actual re-import happens when CodexBar.app (with proper entitlements) refreshes. Same behaviour as `codexbar cache clear --cookies` which also clears without importing.

## Related

- Issue: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/issues/2260
- Settings PR: https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2264

target.title: Migrate ClaudeOAuthRefreshFailureGate fingerprint override to a task-local scope
target.body:
## Summary
Migrate `ClaudeOAuthRefreshFailureGate`'s fingerprint-provider test override off the unsynchronized
process-global `nonisolated(unsafe) static var fingerprintProviderOverride` onto a task-local scope,
mirroring `KeychainAccessPreflight`. Part of #2204.

## Changes
- Replace the static + its `setFingerprintProviderOverrideForTesting` setter with a
  `FingerprintProviderOverrideStore` (`@unchecked Sendable`), a `@TaskLocal` store, and sync + async
  `withFingerprintProviderOverrideForTesting` scopes. `currentFingerprint()` now reads the task-local store.
- The non-macOS stub gains the matching `with…` scopes (loose `(() -> Any?)?` — `AuthFingerprint` is
  macOS-only, as with the prior setter stub).
- Move the ~10 test call sites from `set…{ }` / `defer set…(nil)` to the scoped
  `with…{ provider } operation: { … }` form (unblocks-on-fingerprint-change semantics preserved — the
  provider closure captures the mutated `var` by reference).

## Validation
- `make check` → 0 violations / 1465 files.
- Full suite, contract config (`GROUP_SIZE=4 TIMEOUT=120 RETRY=0`): 660 selections / 165 groups, all
  pass (one keychain-live-proof group timed out under local concurrent-build load and recovered;
  re-run isolated = 4 suites pass in 0.79s — unrelated to this diff). Migrated
  `ClaudeOAuthRefreshFailureGateTests` pass clean in 0.038s.
- Behavior-neutral: overrides were never written outside `…ForTesting` seams; task-local scoping
  eliminates the unsynchronized global rather than locking it.

## Related
- Part of https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/issues/2204 · follows #2239, #2240.

## Out of scope
- Remaining #2204 seams (`CookieHeaderCache`, `KeychainAccessGate`) — separate PRs. No account/auth-file
  behavior changes. Screenshots not applicable (non-UI).

## Notes
- No CHANGELOG entry — internal test synchronization only.


## Real-behavior proof

Fresh build from this PR head (`bd23e63`), then the migrated `ClaudeOAuthRefreshFailureGateTests` suite run under **ThreadSanitizer** — the `@TaskLocal` `FingerprintProviderOverrideStore` is per-task-isolated by construction, so this confirms no data race remains on the override path the old `nonisolated(unsafe) static var` raced on. Swift 6.3.3, arm64 macOS.

**Zero remaining callers of the removed setter** (repo-wide); the task-local scope is the sole override path:

```
$ grep -rn "setFingerprintProviderOverrideForTesting" Sources Tests
(no matches — 0 call sites)
$ grep -rc "withFingerprintProviderOverrideForTesting" Tests   # scoped call sites
10
```

**ThreadSanitizer — full migrated suite:**

```
$ swift test --sanitize=thread --filter "ClaudeOAuthRefreshFailureGateTests"
Build complete! (94.69s)
✔ Suite ClaudeOAuthRefreshFailureGateTests passed after 0.023 seconds.
✔ Test run with 11 tests in 1 suite passed after 0.024 seconds.
```

ThreadSanitizer reported **0 data races**. The migration removes the unsynchronized process-global rather than locking it, so parallel test execution can no longer interleave a write and read on shared override state.

target.title: Fix Claude usage parsing for secondary rate-limit notices
target.body:
## Summary
Fixes a Claude CLI `/usage` parsing bug where CodexBar reports:

```text
Could not parse Claude usage: Claude CLI usage endpoint is rate limited right now. Please try again later.
```

even though Claude Code rendered valid session and weekly usage data.

## What happened
CodexBar drives Claude Code in a PTY and sends `/usage`. In the reported case, the captured panel contained valid quota data:

```text
Current session
3% used

Current week (all models)
11% used
```

but later in the same panel Claude also rendered a non-fatal secondary notice:

```text
Per-model breakdown unavailable (rate limited -- try again in a moment)
```

CodexBar was matching `rate limited` anywhere in the captured output and treating the entire `/usage` scrape as failed. That was too broad: the primary quota data was available and should have been parsed.

## Fix
- Treat Claude CLI rate-limit text as fatal only when no usable `Current session` quota value was rendered.
- Continue parsing session/week usage when only a secondary section, such as per-model breakdown, is rate limited.
- Add a regression test covering valid session/week data plus a secondary rate-limit notice.

## Validation
- Xcode diagnostics: clean for touched files
- Xcode build: passed
- SwiftFormat lint on touched files: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed
- `make check`: portable checks passed, then blocked by sandbox when creating `.build/lint-tools`
- `swift test --filter ClaudeCLIScopedWeeklyUsageTests`: blocked by SwiftPM manifest sandboxing (`sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted`)
